body.estimand_functional: For every \(N\geq K\) and every feasible positive fixed-count vector \(\mathbf n\), under \(Z\sim\mathbb P_{\mathbf n}^{\mathrm{sa}}\), \(\rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}=\sup_{Y\in\mathcal S_N(F)}\operatorname{tr}\{W\operatorname{Cov}_Z(C\widehat{\bar Y}\mid Y)\}\) for every empirical marginal collection \(F\) if and only if \(C^{\mathsf T}WC\in\mathcal R_K\).

sampling_model.design: The headline cone, Loewner, omnibus, and two-arm results use the uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign law: each arm \(a\) receives a prescribed positive count \(n_a\), \(n_{\mathrm u}=N-\sum_a n_a\) units may remain unassigned, and all labelled allocations with those cell counts are equiprobable.  The nonexchangeable balanced-kernel problem is separate and remains explicitly restricted to \(K\mid N\), \(n=N/K\), and no unassigned units.
sampling_model.units: The \(N\) units and all \(K\) potential outcomes per unit are fixed; there is no super-population sampling.  In the two-arm comparator, simple sampling is itself part of the randomized assignment mechanism, not sampling from a superpopulation.
sampling_model.treatment: The assignment vector \(Z\) is the sole random object.  It follows the known uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign law for the headline results or a known admissible nonexchangeable balanced law \(p\) only in the balanced-kernel extension.
sampling_model.overlap: Every reported arm has \(n_a\geq1\), hence known positive marginal assignment probability \(n_a/N\); the unassigned cell may have probability zero or \(n_{\mathrm u}/N\).  The Aronow--Green--Lee equivalence uses at least two treated and two control units as in its cited finite setup.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The structural theorems condition on the armwise empirical marginal laws \(F\).  Their common-rank value is an oracle sharp endpoint; estimation of the marginal laws and its asymptotics are outside this result.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Equation (2) gives the finite oracle variance for sequential simple sampling followed by treatment selection, and Lemma 1 makes the comonotone cross-potential covariance the sharp upper endpoint.
An integer program computes a worst-case copula for broad designs and estimators.
Multi-marginal optimal transport gives exact identified sets for general quadratic cross-world objectives.
The design-based covariance framework permits arbitrary multi-arm contrast matrices under complete randomization.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The fixed-count covariance lemma and Theorem 2

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Supermodular expectations are monotone in concordance for distributions with fixed marginals.
The identity permutation is optimal for a Robinson similarity and dissimilarity when one is Toeplitz.
Isotone imputation converges to a least-favourable two-arm limiting experiment.

body.tldr: Under every uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign design with positive arm counts and an optional unassigned remainder, the common-rank potential-outcome completion is universally least favourable for the scalarized covariance loss \(\operatorname{tr}\{W\operatorname{Cov}_Z(C\widehat{\bar Y})\}\) if and only if \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\) is a graph Laplacian.  The count-independent \(O(K^2)\) certificate has an exact \(2/N\) regret identity and a one-success counterexample for every feasible design outside the cone.  Full covariance dominance occurs only for two nonzero opposite columns of \(C\).  The two-arm result exactly recovers the finite Aronow--Green--Lee sample-then-treat law, Equation (2), and its comonotone oracle endpoint.  On the separate \(K\mid N\) balanced-kernel domain, finite cut copositivity is exact and decidable for algebraic inputs, while polynomial recognition and the minimal complete witness alphabet remain open.

project_justification.gap: Sharp rank completion is analytic for the two-arm difference-in-means estimator, whereas generalized causal-bootstrap work uses integer programming for broad designs and estimators.  The literature does not state the exact contrast-geometry boundary at which one common-rank completion remains universally least favourable for every positive fixed-count multi-arm sample-and-assign experiment, nor the boundary for dominance of the full contrast covariance.  On the realizable nonexchangeable balanced-kernel domain, polynomial-time recognition and a minimal-alphabet certificate remain open.
project_justification.niche: The object is neither a generic transport solver nor another conservative covariance estimator.  It is a design-computable graph-Laplacian cone invariant to unequal positive allocation counts and an unassigned remainder, a two-opposite-columns classification for joint covariance dominance, a full finite recovery of the canonical two-arm oracle formula, and an exact cut-copositivity representation on the distinct balanced moment-polytope domain modulo common unit relabelling.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the uniform fixed-count covariance identity, proves the graph-Laplacian equivalence by finite rearrangement and a one-success necessity witness valid for every feasible count vector, classifies the Loewner case, and preserves two exact \(K=3,N=6\) audits.  It also proves equality of the sequential Aronow--Green--Lee design and the uniform three-cell law and derives their variance formula term by term.  For general balanced kernels with \(K\mid N\), it proves finite cut copositivity and a terminating exact algebraic algorithm while leaving polynomial complexity and the minimal complete alphabet explicit residual questions.

body.related_work: Aronow, Green, and Lee give a finite two-stage sample-then-treat variance formula and prove that its upper endpoint is attained by comonotone potential outcomes.  The two-arm proposition proves that their sequential randomization is exactly the uniform treated--control--unassigned allocation law, derives their Equation (2) from the fixed-count covariance identity term by term, and uses their Lemma 1 only for sharp comonotone attainment.  Imbens and Menzel use isotone completion for a least-favourable two-arm limiting experiment.  Zhao and Ding supply the arbitrary-contrast complete-randomization covariance framework; the present result extends the relevant identity to arbitrary positive fixed counts with an optional unassigned remainder and optimizes its unidentified cross-arm terms.  Tchen's supermodular order is consistent with the rearrangement mechanism, while the proof here gives the finite permutation argument and the graph-Laplacian necessity witness directly.  Gao, Ge, and Qian formulate general quadratic cross-world extrema as multi-marginal transport, and Brennan et al. compute generalized causal-bootstrap completions by integer programming.  On the explicitly balanced \(K\mid N\) kernel domain, the separate theorem instead gives an exact finite cut-copositivity characterization.  Laurent and Seminaroti's Robinson--Toeplitz result is a sufficient identity-optimal class for a two-matrix quadratic assignment problem, not the necessary-and-sufficient or polynomial recognition result sought here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The graph-Laplacian certificate concerns a prespecified scalar covariance loss \(W\) and does not turn that endpoint into a sharp matrix-valued covariance bound.  Except for a vector-rescaled pairwise contrast, no single common-rank completion dominates every linear combination simultaneously.  The arbitrary-count result assumes a known uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign law and oracle knowledge of all armwise empirical marginals; it does not supply plug-in marginal estimation or Wald coverage.  For general nonexchangeable balanced kernels, the theorem remains restricted to \(K\mid N\) with equal exhaustive counts and uses factorial permutation and exponential support enumeration; polynomial recognition, binary completeness, and the minimal complete alphabet remain unresolved.
body.honest_scope: The arbitrary-count cone theorem follows from the fixed-count design covariance identity plus a finite rearrangement proof and a contrast-geometry necessity argument; novelty lies in the causal contrast cone, its count invariance, and the Loewner boundary, not in a new general dependence inequality.  The Aronow--Green--Lee proposition is an exact finite oracle equivalence and does not claim new marginal-estimation asymptotics.  The six-unit propositions are arithmetic audit certificates.  The general balanced-kernel result is explicitly confined to \(K\mid N\), equal exhaustive counts, and admissible covariance tensors induced by balanced assignment laws.  Its exhaustive exact algorithm applies to real-algebraic inputs; no polynomial runtime, hardness classification, binary completeness, or minimal-alphabet theorem is claimed.
body.interpretation: For a uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign experiment, a practitioner only inspects the off-diagonal signs of \(C^{\mathsf T}WC\).  Nonpositive signs certify one-sort least-favourable completion regardless of unequal positive arm counts or the number of unassigned units.  Any positive entry names two arms on which separating two unique successes strictly improves the loss by \(2H_{ab}/[N(N-1)]\).  Matrix-valued conservativeness is much rarer: it occurs exactly when \(C\) has two nonzero opposite columns.  The orthonormal omnibus system is scalar-valid for every count vector but, for \(K>2\), is not Loewner-valid.  The nonexchangeable balanced-kernel extension remains a separate \(K\mid N\) problem with an exact but exhaustive copositivity audit.
